task.description: WF-03 Step 1 for run WF03-GH797-20260816: root-cause diagnosis (diagnosis-as-design) for the process-gap fix captured in ISS-0710 / GH-797. Background (already established in Step 0.5): GH-797 is a process/duplicate issue. ADHOC-prm-reqctl-status-20260816 was dispatched to mark PRM-02/03/04/05 RELEASED in docs/requirements.yaml, but that work had ALREADY been completed independently by WF02-prm02-05-20260816 (PR #795; PRM-02/03/04/05 confirmed `status: RELEASED` at origin/main HEAD). The ADHOC's pre-flight correctly detected already-RELEASED status and aborted with BLOCKER, but only AFTER step-00 had already created the housekeeping branch `housekeeping/reqctl-status-stale-20260816` and a setup stash — i.e. an ADHOC dispatched against an outdated view of the repo reached step-00 before discovering the target work was done. CONFIRM/REFINE this root cause by reading ISS-0710.json and the GH-797 body, then DEFINE the fix approach for Step 3 (BACKEND-DEV) precisely: a lightweight dispatch-time short-circuit check — e.g. `reqctl.py show <id>` or `git show HEAD:<file>` for the affected requirement IDs — to be performed BEFORE an ADHOC run's step-00 creates any branch, so an already-completed target short-circuits with a BLOCKER before any branch/stash is created. Specify WHERE the check belongs (candidate: ORCHESTRATOR.md §5 ad-hoc workflow construction and/or the ADHOC dispatch template in core-directives.md — confirm the exact file/section), WHAT the check runs, and WHAT the short-circuit behavior must be. Document this in the handoff result as the fix spec for Step 3. Do NOT implement the fix yourself.
acceptance_criteria: Root cause confirmed/refined against ISS-0710.json and the GH-797 body
Fix approach for Step 3 fully specified: exact file/section to change, the exact dispatch-time check, and the short-circuit behavior (BLOCKER before branch creation)

what_it_runs: At ADHOC construction time, BEFORE dispatching step-00:
1. git fetch origin (the check MUST read the true current state, not the stale local view - this is the exact failure mode being eliminated).

2. For each requirement ID targeted by the ADHOC's desired end state (e.g. PRM-02/03/04/05), read its status from origin/main: python tools/reqctl.py show <id> (project's canonical reader; exits non-zero on missing ID), or if the working tree is not at origin/main, git show origin/main:docs/requirements.yaml and parse the entry.
3. Compare each target's status against the ADHOC's declared desired end-state (for this class of run: RELEASED).

4. Verdict is exit-code-only per section 8a 'Judge this gate by the exit code only' and the Never-Satisfy-a-Gate-by-Editing-What-It-Measures directive: exit 0 if NO target is already at the desired end-state; non-zero (BLOCKER) if ANY target already is.
short_circuit_behavior: If ANY target requirement is already at the ADHOC's desired end-state at origin/main HEAD:

1. ORCH does NOT create or dispatch step-00 - no branch, no stash, no git-setup. This is the primary control; the existing in-run pre-flight ('if already RELEASED, STOP and FAIL with BLOCKER (someone else fixed it)') stays as defense-in-depth for the dispatch-to-execution race window.

2. Abort the ADHOC with result.status = BLOCKED (legal value) and a BLOCKER issue entry naming the already-done requirement IDs and, where known, the run/PR that delivered them (here: WF02-prm02-05-20260816 / PR #795).
3. Log: <ISO8601> | DISPATCH_STALE | <run-id> | --- | ORCH | BLOCKER - target already at <status> at origin/main HEAD (<delivering run/PR>) - ADHOC short-circuited before step-00.
4. No cleanup is required because no branch or stash is ever created.
If the check passes (no target already at end-state): proceed with normal section 5 construction and dispatch step-00.
fix_spec.scope: Applies to every ADHOC whose desired end state is a status change in a tracked YAML/data file (e.g. docs/requirements.yaml) - i.e. any ADHOC whose end-state precondition could already be satisfied at origin/main.
